brief.headline: The exchange has still not printed a new official - the Monday ring runs after this compile - but the overnight information set tilted modestly toward the bulls on the macro leg while leaving the supply cap exactly where it was: Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory drew a further 12,000 tonnes to 886,000 tonnes, and two sharply weak US demand prints pushed the market to begin trading the END of the Federal Reserve's hiking cycle, weakening the dollar - while the same research note repeats that the Gulf restart is running faster than expected and caps the upside.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: NOT THE PRICE, BUT THE MACRO READ, AND THAT IS THE FIRST FACT OF THE DAY. This compiles on Monday 17-August before the ring. The 13:20 London official has not yet printed, so the latest published settlement is still Friday 14-August: cash $3,248.00, three-month $3,246.00, a $2.00 backwardation, and warehouse stock of 248,300 tonnes after a 33rd consecutive daily draw. Both the English and German Westmetall overviews were fetched cache-busted and both returned the same 14-August board; Trading Economics separately still marks 14-August. Any dashboard showing a newer aluminium official right now would be inventing one. The next genuine price information arrives at 13:20 London today.

THE MACRO LEG TURNED OVERNIGHT AND IT TURNED SUPPORTIVE. SMM's 17-August morning minutes report that US July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month - the largest decline in more than a year, against expectations of a small increase - with the core control group excluding autos, building materials and fuel down 0.4%, the worst reading since January 2025. The preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment index for August came in at 51 against an expected 54.5. SMM's own conclusion is that consecutively weak data significantly lowered expectations of a September Federal Reserve rate HIKE and that the market has begun to trade the end of the hiking cycle, leaving the dollar index under pressure and providing macro support for LME metals. CME FedWatch is quoted at 67.5% for no change through September against 32.5% for a cumulative 25 basis points of tightening. Note the two-sidedness honestly: the same prints are weak US END-DEMAND, which is not a bullish fact for physical consumption.

THE INVENTORY EVIDENCE EXTENDED FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE PUBLICATION. Chinese aluminium ingot inventory in the major consumption regions stood at 886,000 tonnes as of Monday, down 12,000 tonnes from last Thursday and down 31,000 tonnes from last Monday. That is a second, independent pool drawing alongside seven weeks of LME warrant draws, and it is now a run of observations rather than a single reading. The honest counterweight sits in the same document: China's July aluminium billet operating rate hit a year-to-date high of 58.3%, billet processing fees have fallen BELOW the industry's average production cost line, and SMM expects the operating rate to retreat to around 56.9% in August - which diverts metal back into ingot and is the cleanest mechanism by which the destock could stall.

WHAT TO WATCH TODAY, IN ORDER. First, the 13:20 London official and specifically the $3,229.50 wave (iv) low, $18.50 below Friday's cash settlement - the single explicit invalidation on the short-term count. Second, whether the front-end backwardation survives a third session; two consecutive days is the first two-day prompt premium since 04-August. Third, the stock line, where a 34th consecutive draw would extend the divergence between falling warrant and a softening flat price. Fourth, the monthly carbon settlement window - prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle around the 17th-18th, and the fluoride lines have already moved against smelters.

lme.commentary: THERE IS STILL NO NEW LME SESSION TO COMMENT ON - THIS COMPILES ON MONDAY 17-AUGUST BEFORE THE 13:20 LONDON RING. The 14-August official therefore remains the latest published board: cash $3,248.00, three-month $3,246.00, a $2.00 backwardation and stock of 248,300 tonnes after a 33rd consecutive draw. THE THREE-SESSION SEQUENCE THAT PRECEDED IT IS WORTH RESTATING BECAUSE TODAY WILL BE JUDGED AGAINST IT: cash fell $125.00 (-3.71%) from the 11-August high of $3,373.00 across 12, 13 and 14-August, on three dated public supply-relief facts - a Gulf smelter guided back to pre-incident hot metal in Q1-2027 from about 18% of capacity, an Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 by a state support package covering up to 590,000 t/y, and the largest alumina refinery outside China returning to full rate after a three-day gas outage. Through all three sessions the stock line kept falling and the front end kept its premium, which is why this desk has read the decline as a repricing of the FORWARD supply story rather than a loosening of the PROMPT one. SMM'S 17-AUGUST MINUTES ADD THE INTRADAY SHAPE OF FRIDAY, PUBLISHED THIS MORNING, AND IT IS MILDLY CONSTRUCTIVE. LME aluminium opened $3,238.50, traded a high of $3,260.00 and a low of $3,221.50 and closed at $3,245.00 on SMM's basis, up 0.22% - a small bullish candle that found support at the 20-day moving average near $3,243.86 with the 5-day at $3,268.58 capping from above. Critically, volume PULLED BACK while OPEN INTEREST INCREASED, which SMM characterises as bulls adding positions rather than length liquidating; on the Shanghai contract the mirror image occurred, with open interest falling notably on bears reducing positions. THE TEST TODAY IS NARROW AND EXPLICIT. First, the $3,229.50 wave (iv) low, $18.50 below Friday's cash settlement, is the single stated invalidation on the short-term count. regional.basis: Q3-2026 SETTLED at $395/t CIF Japan (S&P Global Platts, assessed 06-Jul-2026 off concluded trades), against the Q2-2026 settlement of $350-353/t - up 11.9-12.9% quarter-on-quarter and the highest quarterly Japanese premium of the past decade, last exceeded in Q3-2014 at $404/t. Negotiation offers through the Q3 round ran $440-480/t before settling at $395/t, which remains the single most useful piece of public context for the Q4 round: the gap between opening offers and the settled number was roughly $50-85/t. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND THIS IS A SUNDAY. A dedicated search this run (16-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here - assessment agencies do not publish at the weekend either - so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. THE Q4 ARGUMENT MOVED AGAIN THIS WEEKEND AND IT MOVED FURTHER TOWARD THE BUYER, THOUGH NOT UNIFORMLY. SMM's 16-August review states that 18% of the Gulf smelter's 1,262 pots have been restarted, that the pace has been FASTER than the market previously expected, and that the supply tightness premium priced in earlier now faces giveback pressure with upside capped by resumption expectations. That is a research house saying explicitly what a buyer would otherwise have to argue. It follows three dated relief facts from last week - the Q1-2027 Gulf recovery guidance, the Australian smelter power settlement and the Alunorte return to full rate. WHAT THE SELLER GAINED IN THE SAME DOCUMENT, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING: Chinese aluminium ingot social inventory is destocking too, at 898,000 t on Thursday, down 19,000 t from Monday and 35,000 t on the prior Thursday, with global ingot destocking described as unchanged - the first independent corroboration of seven weeks of exchange draws. A seller can now point at two inventory pools rather than one. None of this is a premium assessment and none of it is being treated as one here.

CIF Japan spot reference. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND THIS IS A SUNDAY. A dedicated search this run (16-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here - assessment agencies do not publish at the weekend either - so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. The spot reference sits $25/t BELOW the settled Q3 quarterly number of $395/t, and that gap remains the most concrete public anchor available for the Q4 negotiation that conventionally opens in late August - a buyer can point at it without needing a forecast. The yen closed 14-August at 159.326 per dollar, marginally firmer, which trims rather than adds to the local-currency cost of a dollar-denominated premium, but a 0.11% currency move is immaterial next to a $25/t spot-to-quarterly gap. THE CONSEQUENTIAL WEEKEND DEVELOPMENT FOR A JAPANESE BUYER IS THE RESTART PACE: SMM's 16-August review describes the Gulf smelter's resumption as faster than the market previously expected at 18% of 1,262 pots, and concludes that the earlier supply tightness premium faces giveback pressure. Japan draws heavily on Gulf and Australian units, so a faster-than-expected Gulf recovery is directly relevant to the Q4 round in a way that neither the Brazilian alumina episode nor the Australian power settlement was.

A dedicated search this run (15-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here, so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. THE EUROPEAN CONTEXT SOFTENED AT THE MARGIN THIS SESSION. European gas TTF marked EUR 61.43/MWh on the 14-August board, UP 1.70% and the largest single-session move in the energy leg this week, which pressures the European cost curve at the same time as the metal price fell $31.00 - a double-sided margin compression for the EU fleet. The Slovalco restart of about +75,000 t/y remains funded for Q4-2026 and is the region's only near-term supply addition.

A dedicated search this run (15-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here, so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. The billet premium is a value-added conversion margin stacked on top of the P1020 ingot premium, so it responds to European extrusion demand rather than to the LME front end. Nothing dated after the carried assessment has published. The EU 6% duty on non-preferential third-country P1020 is the structural floor under any duty-paid European number and is unchanged.

Platts Midwest US Transaction premium. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. A dedicated search this run (15-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here, so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. THE TARIFF ARITHMETIC MOVED EVEN THOUGH THE ASSESSMENT DID NOT, AND THIS IS THE ONE US NUMBER THAT REFRESHES EVERY SESSION. At the 14-August cash of $3,248.00 the Section 232 leg is 50% x $3,248.00 = $1,624.00/t, DOWN $15.50 on yesterday purely because metal fell. Against the carried $2,380/t transaction level the tariff accounts for roughly 68% of the total. Two thirds of a US delivered premium is policy arithmetic that changes with the LME price, not a measure of American physical tightness, and any US-facing analysis that treats the whole number as a market signal is reading the tax as though it were the market.

US Midwest duty-paid delivered. PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. A dedicated search this run (15-Aug-2026) returned no public assessment dated after the mark carried here, so the last public mark is carried at its assessment date rather than re-stated as if it were fresh. US Midwest duty-paid is the tariff-inflated companion to the transaction row and carries the same $1,624.00/t Section 232 leg at the 14-August cash price. The domestic supply pipeline continues to build against it: Century's Mt. Holly has been at full capacity since 27-July for the first time since 2015 and Magnitude 7 Metals targets a partial New Madrid restart before year-end. More domestic metal behind a 50% tariff wall is the mechanism by which a US premium eventually falls without the tariff changing at all.

drivers.text: A research house has now said out loud what the buyer's case needed - the earlier tightness premium faces giveback pressure — SMM's aluminium weekly review published 16-August states that 18% of the Gulf smelter's 1,262 pots have been restarted following the 28-March attack, that production is expected to recover to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027, and - the operative clause for a premium negotiation - that the pace of production resumption has been FASTER THAN THE MARKET PREVIOUSLY EXPECTED, concluding that the supply tightness premium priced in earlier now faces giveback pressure and that upside room is capped to some extent by production resumption expectations. It also discloses that the associated alumina refinery recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July. For the Q4 round this converts a buyer's inference into a citable third-party statement.
drivers.source: SMM via AL Circle - Mild inflation pullback eases macro anxiety, production resumptions accelerate (16-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: The seller's inventory argument doubled in strength - Chinese social stock is destocking alongside LME warrant — The same 16-August review reports China's aluminium ingot social inventory at 898,000 tonnes as of Thursday, DOWN 19,000 tonnes from Monday of the same week and DOWN 35,000 tonnes from the previous Thursday, describing the global aluminium ingot destocking trend as unchanged in the short term. Set against LME warrant at 248,300 tonnes after 33 consecutive daily draws, a seller can now show two structurally different inventory pools in two different regulatory regimes drawing at the same time - which is materially harder to attribute to warehouse financing than a single exchange series. The honest qualifier, from the same source: destocking is expected to continue but to SLOW in the second half of the month.
drivers.source: SMM via AL Circle - aluminium weekly review, China social inventory (16-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: The front end held a backwardation two sessions running and there has been no ring since to break it — Cash settled $3,248.00 against a three-month of $3,246.00 on 14-August, a $2.00 BACKWARDATION narrowed from $4.00 but intact for a second consecutive session - the first two-day prompt premium since 04-August. Through the first half of August the front end repeatedly flickered into a prompt premium and surrendered it the next day, so two consecutive days was a different signal. Because the LME does not trade at the weekend, that structure is what a Q4 negotiator carries into Monday unchanged. Proportion cuts against over-reading it: $2.00 is 0.06% of cash and it narrowed rather than widened. The specific test is whether it survives a third session.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME official settlements, 14-Aug-2026 board (English and German overviews, both cache-busted)

drivers.text: The tariff leg is unchanged this run because the metal price is unchanged - the reminder that two thirds of a US duty-paid number is arithmetic — The Section 232 rate on aluminium articles is re-verified at 50% this run, with 25% on derivative articles applied to full customs value since the 06-April-2026 modification, and Annex I-C carve-outs at 15% for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. At the 14-August cash official of $3,248.00 the tariff leg computes to $1,624.00/t and is unchanged over the weekend for the simple reason that no new cash official has printed. Against the carried $2,380/t US transaction level that is roughly 68% of the total. A US-delivered premium therefore moves every session the metal moves, whatever the physical market is doing - and does not move at all on a day the exchange is shut.
drivers.source: Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg / White & Case - Section 232 aluminium tariffs, 50% articles and 25% derivatives on full customs value

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE ALUNORTE EPISODE HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A FIFTH RUN - the events are recorded, the price is not invented. This is a Sunday compile and seaborne alumina transactions are not reported at the weekend, so the absence is expected rather than surprising. THE SUPPLY EVENT RESOLVED AND HAS STAYED RESOLVED. Norsk Hydro announced on 13-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - is ramping back to FULL capacity after Brazil's regulator ANP approved it as a self-importer of natural gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement was reached with gas supplier CELBA. The disruption ran three days from the 11-August disclosure of a cut to 50%. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes with a guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. No newer development published over the weekend. THE HONEST READ REMAINS THAT THE COST CONSEQUENCE WAS NEVER OBSERVED: the outage never lasted long enough to produce a public seaborne price print and now probably never will. Roughly 3 Mt/y annualised off the balance for three days is a rounding error against a 145 Mt/y global market. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a rally. MARGIN CONTEXT AT AN UNCHANGED METAL PRICE: against the 14-August three-month official of $3,246.00 the FOB mark sits at about 11.0% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.2%, both unchanged from yesterday because neither leg moved. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a clear TAILWIND to smelter economics. NEW CONTEXT FROM THE GULF THIS WEEKEND: SMM reports that the Gulf producer's alumina refinery recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July after its H1-2026 production fell significantly year-on-year - a second refinery returning supply to a market that has just absorbed the Alunorte scare without printing a price.

prices.label: Alumina API / Platts FOB Australia
prices.note: Platts FOB Australia - NO PUBLIC MARK AT AN AUGUST 2026 DATE. The Platts alumina index and the Fastmarkets MB-ALU-0002 index are subscription products and are not publicly quotable. The last independently verifiable public Platts level is $304/mt on 15-Apr-2026, with Q1-2026 averaging $306.91/mt (-2.82% quarter-on-quarter); the $330/t carried here derives from a 26-Jun reference in S&P Global coverage. The value and date are CARRIED UNCHANGED and are explicitly stale - the two SMM-reported transactions above ($356/mt FOB East Australia dealt 05-Aug, $365/mt CIF Malaysia dealt 07-Aug) are far fresher and should be read as the live market. Both sit well above this carried index level, so the direction of travel since late June has been UP, and the Alunorte cut points the same way. A USEFUL INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK REMAINS South32's FY26 operating report, which gives average REALISED alumina prices of $363/t at Worsley (down 30% year-on-year from $518/t) and $356/t at Brazil Alumina (down 36% from $555/t) across the full financial year to June 2026. Those are annual realisations on a different basis from a spot index and must not be blended into this row, but they independently place the market in the mid-$350s to low-$360s and confirm how far alumina has fallen year-on-year.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply sits at half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way.

prices.note: CME-listed alumina futures settle against the Platts FOB Australia index. Carried at its stated date; no public settlement series is quotable without a subscription. Directionally every available signal still points the same way - the two SMM-reported physical trades this month ($356/mt FOB East Australia, $365/mt CIF Malaysia), the RMB 37/mt month-on-month rise in Chinese production cost, and the Alunorte reduction to 50 percent now in its third day with no restart date. This row is carried, not marked, and should be read as stale.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review. THE NEXT EDITION IS DUE TODAY on the publication's Thursday cadence and had not printed at this 03:40 London compile, so the row is carried rather than marked. SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION FROM THE 11-AUGUST COST REVIEW: imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT CARRIED FROM LAST RUN: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders; CEO Patrice L'Huillier named Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

prices.label: Caustic soda (China alumina-plant contract, Shanxi)
prices.note: CNY 2,090/t delivered, 50% ion-membrane liquid on a 100% NaOH basis - the JULY purchase price at Shanxi alumina plants, held flat month-on-month. THE VALUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED because August contracts have not settled and no new public mark was returned this run. GUIDANCE CARRIED AND IT IS WHY THE TREND FLAG IS UP: SMM's alumina cost review states that Shanxi caustic soda long-term contract prices are EXPECTED TO RISE BY RMB 50/mt in August, while Guangxi prices are set to DECLINE FURTHER BY RMB 150/mt. That is an explicit regional divergence, not a national move: the north tightens slightly, the south loosens and widens its cost advantage. SMM's assessment of the aggregate effect is that caustic 'had limited impact on alumina production costs' in July and will show 'overall narrow fluctuations' in August. AN EXPECTATION IS NOT A SETTLEMENT: the RMB 50/mt is carried as guidance in this note only and has not been written into the value, which stays at the last settled July figure.

prices.label: Lime / quicklime (China average)
prices.note: China average quicklime for alumina refining, carried at its stated date - no newer public assessment was returned this run and this row has no weekly public series, so gaps stay gaps. Lime is a small share of refinery cash cost and is not a swing factor in the current cost picture; SMM's 11-August cost decomposition attributes July's RMB 37/mt rise to bauxite, with caustic regionally divergent and energy slightly lower, and does not identify lime as a driver.

notes: ALUNORTE IS BACK AND HAS STAYED BACK - NO NEW DEVELOPMENT OVER THE WEEKEND. Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte had cut to 50% of capacity after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability, and announced on 13-August that it is ramping back to full capacity following ANP approval to act as a self-importer of gas and a temporary terminal-access agreement with CELBA. Lost production is put at 100,000-120,000 tonnes and the guided potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million - covering both lost tonnes and gas bought above contract price - is unchanged. A dedicated search this Sunday found nothing dated after 14-August.

THE WORD THAT STILL MATTERS IN THE COMPANY'S OWN LANGUAGE IS 'TEMPORARY'. The terminal-access agreement with CELBA is explicitly temporary and sits alongside regulatory approval for the refinery to act as a self-importer of natural gas. The outage is resolved on a run-rate basis but the underlying gas arrangement is not permanently settled. A 6.3 Mt/y refinery is large enough that any recurrence is material to the seaborne balance, so the thing to watch is a further disclosure converting the temporary arrangement into a durable one - or failing to.

THE EPISODE PASSED WITHOUT REGISTERING ON ANY PUBLIC PRICE SERIES, AND THAT IS ITSELF THE FINDING. No public seaborne alumina transaction dated after 07-August has been located across five consecutive runs. Three days of a 3 Mt/y annualised outage is about 50-60 kt on a pro-rata basis, reconciling broadly with the company's own 100-120 kt figure for the full reduced-rate period, against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market. The prior expectation stated here so it could be checked - that the episode would leave no mark - has so far held.

A SECOND REFINERY IS ALSO RETURNING, WHICH IS THE NEW ALUMINA FACT OF THE WEEKEND. SMM's 16-August review discloses that the Gulf producer's alumina refinery recovered to 50% of pre-incident levels in early July, after H1-2026 production fell significantly year-on-year. Alumina supply is therefore being restored from two directions at once while the metal price falls, which is why the alumina-to-metal ratio remains a tailwind to smelter margin rather than a threat to it.

SMM's cost work identifies imported bauxite as the core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost in July, citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments alongside slow domestic Chinese mine resumption. That pressure is about ore supply and freight rather than about any single refinery's gas contract, so it is unaffected by the Alunorte resolution and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board.

headlines.title: THE MARKET HAS STARTED TRADING THE END OF THE HIKING CYCLE, AND THAT IS THE OVERNIGHT CHANGE. SMM's 17-August morning minutes report US July retail sales down 0.6% month-on-month - the largest decline in more than a year, against market expectations of a slight increase - with the core control group excluding autos, building materials and gasoline stations down 0.4%, the worst performance since January 2025. The preliminary August University of Michigan consumer sentiment index printed 51 against 54.5 expected. SMM's stated conclusion is that consecutively weak economic data significantly lowered market expectations for a September Federal Reserve rate HIKE, that the market has begun to trade expectations for the end of the hiking cycle, and that the dollar index is under pressure - which it describes as providing macro support for LME metals. CME FedWatch is quoted at 67.5% for no change through September against 32.5% for a cumulative 25 basis points; through October, 53.3% no change, 39.8% for 25 basis points and 6.8% for 50. READ IT BOTH WAYS: the dollar leg is supportive, but a 0.6% fall in US retail sales is weak end-demand in the largest consumer economy on earth, and aluminium is a consumption metal.

THE SECOND INVENTORY POOL DREW AGAIN AND IT IS NOW A RUN, NOT A READING. SMM's 17-August minutes put aluminium ingot inventory in China's major consumption regions at 886,000 tonnes as of Monday, DOWN 12,000 tonnes from last Thursday and DOWN 31,000 tonnes from last Monday - against 898,000 tonnes reported on Thursday in the 16-August weekly. Set beside 33 consecutive LME warrant draws to 248,300 tonnes, two structurally different inventory pools have now been shown drawing together across successive publications. This is the single most important analytical development of the past fortnight and it strengthened rather than faded on repetition: the standing objection to exchange draws - that warrant can leave for financing reasons unrelated to consumption - simply does not travel to Chinese social inventory.

THE BILLET NUMBERS ARE THE CLEANEST MECHANISM BY WHICH THE DESTOCK COULD STALL, AND THEY WERE PUBLISHED IN THE SAME DOCUMENT AS THE DESTOCK. China's July aluminium billet operating rate rose 1.1 percentage points month-on-month to 58.3%, up 5.2 percentage points year-on-year - a year-to-date high and a high for the period across the past three years, driven by the strength of Q2 processing fees. But SMM reports that as the aluminium price rebounded through July, downstream operating performance and purchase willingness were constrained, billet processing fees pulled back sharply from June highs and have now fallen BELOW the industry's average production cost line, and a small number of billet producers have already chosen to suspend or cut production ahead of time. SMM expects the August operating rate to retreat to around 56.9%. The mechanism matters more than the sentiment: when billet conversion margins go negative, casthouses divert metal back into ingot, relieving ingot scarcity precisely when inventory statistics are being read as proof of tightness.

THE RESTART CHARACTERISATION WAS REPEATED VERBATIM 24 HOURS LATER, WHICH IS ITSELF INFORMATION. SMM's 17-August overall outlook restates that the UAE producer disclosed resumption progress at its Al Taweelah plant, that 18% of the plant's 1,262 pots have restarted, that the pace of resumption is FASTER than the market had previously expected, and that the previously traded tight-supply premium faces pressure to give back, with upside room capped to some extent by resumption expectations. Pre-incident hot metal is guided for Q1-2027. A publisher restating a characterisation unchanged the following session is standing behind it rather than walking it back, and this is the specific sentence that took roughly $10/t off the top of the MJP Q4 scenario range yesterday.

The latest published official for every metal is therefore Friday's: aluminium cash $3,248.00, three-month $3,246.00, a $2.00 backwardation, stock 248,300 tonnes after a 33rd consecutive draw. SMM's 17-August minutes independently corroborate the Friday close at $3,245.00 on its own basis.

THE ONE PIECE OF NEW POSITIONING EVIDENCE CUTS AGAINST THE LIQUIDATION READING. SMM's 17-August minutes report that in Friday's LME session trading VOLUME pulled back while OPEN INTEREST INCREASED, which the desk characterises as bulls adding positions. On the SHFE side the opposite happened - open interest fell notably, driven mainly by bears reducing positions. Neither observation is decisive on its own, but taken with a front end that held a backwardation through a $60 two-session decline, the weight of evidence is against a disorderly long liquidation and toward a market rotating length rather than shedding it.

CHINA'S JULY CAR RETAIL FELL 20.9% YEAR-ON-YEAR, AND THE MIX IS THE ONLY THING SOFTENING THE BLOW. CPCA data reported by SMM put nationwide passenger vehicle retail at 1.461 million units in July, down 20.9% year-on-year. New energy vehicle retail was 951,000 units, down 3.9% year-on-year, with penetration at 65.1%; conventional internal combustion vehicles were 510,000 units, down 41% year-on-year. Passenger NEV exports ran the other way entirely at 540,000 units, up 147.8% year-on-year. Automotive is one of the largest end-use blocks for aluminium and NEVs carry materially more aluminium per vehicle than combustion cars, so the mix shift and the export surge partially offset the headline. It remains a demand-side fact that belongs on the bear side of the ledger.

CHINESE CREDIT CREATION IS RUNNING MARGINALLY BEHIND LAST YEAR. SMM cites preliminary central bank statistics putting the cumulative increase in aggregate financing to the real economy over the first seven months of 2026 at RMB 22.25 trillion, DOWN RMB 174 billion on the same period last year. Aggregate financing is the broadest available public proxy for Chinese construction and infrastructure activity, which is the single largest end-use block for aluminium globally. The shortfall is small - well under 1% - and should not be over-read, but it does not support a demand-led interpretation of the inventory destock.

A SMALL DEAL THAT ILLUSTRATES A LARGE PROBLEM. SMM reports that Jamaica and Ghana are negotiating a potential US$60 million bauxite-to-alumina supply arrangement that would revive a trading relationship first proposed more than two decades ago. Under the proposed structure Jamaican bauxite would be shipped to the Atlantic Alumina Company refinery at Gramercy, Louisiana for processing into alumina, with the alumina then exported to Ghana for use in its aluminium industry, involving Jamaica's state-owned Jamaica Bauxite Mining and Ghana's integrated aluminium development effort. The tonnage is immaterial against a roughly 145 million tonne per year alumina market. The signal is not: three-continent tolling arrangements of this shape are what an industry builds when ore security rather than refining capacity is the binding constraint, which is the same structural story as the Guinea contract negotiations and the 749% surge in Chinese alumina imports reported for H1-2026.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

status.name: China operators (aggregate)
status.status: At the 45 Mt policy ceiling; July billet operating rate at a year-to-date high of 58.3% but processing fees now below average cost
status.impact: REFRESHED ON THE 16-AUGUST SMM WEEKLY. China's weekly aluminium production was basically stable over the past week and the proportion of liquid aluminium rose 0.11 percentage point week-on-week - a marginal shift toward direct-to-casthouse delivery rather than ingot. Effectively no headroom remains for further Chinese supply growth against the 45 Mt policy ceiling, so the growth is being exported to Indonesia and elsewhere instead. On the demand side the same review places the downstream processing industry in its traditional consumption off-season with operating rates under pressure, and flags that aluminium billet processing fees pulled back, weakening replacement demand for aluminium ingot - the mechanism that could slow the destocking SMM itself expects to continue but decelerate in the second half of the month.
status.update: REFRESHED ON THE 17-AUGUST SMM MINUTES, AND THE NEW DETAIL IS ON THE CASTHOUSE SIDE RATHER THAN THE POTLINE SIDE. China's July aluminium billet operating rate rose 1.1 percentage points month-on-month to 58.3%, up 5.2 percentage points year-on-year - a year-to-date high and a high for the period across the past three years, carried by the strength of Q2 processing fees. That inertia has now broken: as the aluminium price rebounded through July, downstream operating performance and purchase willingness were constrained, billet processing fees pulled back sharply from June highs and have fallen BELOW the industry's average production cost line, and a small number of billet producers chose to suspend or cut production ahead of time. SMM expects the August billet operating rate to retreat to around 56.9%. On the primary side, effectively no headroom remains against the 45 Mt policy ceiling, so growth is being exported to Indonesia and elsewhere. The billet line is the mechanism to watch: negative conversion margins divert metal back into ingot and would slow the very destock the same document reports.

catalysts.text: TODAY'S LME OFFICIAL - THE FIRST NEW PRICE INFORMATION SINCE FRIDAY, AND THE TEST IS SPECIFIC ON TWO LEVELS. FIRST, THE WAVE (iv) LOW AT $3,229.50, now just $18.50 below the cash settlement of $3,248.00. It is the single explicit invalidation on the short-term Elliott count: holding it keeps the impulse-continuation count alive, a decisive close beneath it promotes the bearish alternate and opens $3,205 (wave i) and then $3,159.50 (wave ii). SECOND, WHETHER THE BACKWARDATION SURVIVES A THIRD SESSION. Two consecutive days is the first two-day prompt premium since 04-August; three would make it a trend and the strongest evidence this cycle that the physical market is tightening independently of financial positioning. A slip into contango marks the two-day premium as noise. Watch the stock line alongside: a 34th consecutive draw would extend the divergence. FOR THIRD-PARTY CALIBRATION ONLY, NOT ENDORSEMENT: SMM's published week-ahead range is $3,180-3,330 on LME and RMB 23,600-24,450 on the most-traded SHFE contract, and its 17-August note flags the 20-day moving average near $3,243.86 as the level that caught Friday's session.

TOMORROW: A MAJOR RUSSIAN PRODUCER'S BOARD MEETS TO APPROVE H1-2026 IFRS ACCOUNTS. The board of directors is scheduled to meet on 18-August-2026 to review first-half operational performance and to consider and approve the company's consolidated interim condensed IFRS financial statements. It is the next dated peer-earnings event on the calendar and the first half-year read on the largest producer outside China and the West. The comparison base is public: adjusted EBITDA of US$748 million in H1-2025 against US$786 million in H1-2024, with the EBITDA margin narrowing from 13.8% to 9.9% and a shareholders' loss of US$87 million in H1-2025. Given realised prices across the peer group have risen sharply this year, the interest is in whether that margin compression has reversed - a read on where the industry cost curve actually sits at these metal prices.

THE MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW IS OPEN THIS WEEK - prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle around the 17th-18th. This is the scheduled opportunity to append sourced marks to the input-basket histories for those rows, all of which are currently carried at their June or July cycles and were NOT estimated this run. THE DIRECTIONAL RISK INTO THE WINDOW IS MODESTLY UPWARD: Brent closed 14-August up 1.67% at $88.52, and green coke is a refinery by-product whose price follows crude with a lag. The fluoride lines have already moved that way - cryolite repriced up to RMB 7,500-9,000/t and the August aluminium fluoride tender raised RMB 250/t month-on-month - so a firm carbon settlement would make it two cost groups turning against smelters in the same fortnight.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open against the Q3-2026 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan. A dedicated search this run again returned nothing dated after the 06-July settlement - no producer offers, no negotiation levels, no settlement coverage - so the pending quarter remains a SCENARIO RANGE of $305-395 and not an assessment. It is HELD unchanged from yesterday rather than narrowed again, because the only relevant 17-August input was SMM restating the Gulf restart characterisation verbatim, and a repetition is not new evidence. Sellers retain 33 consecutive LME draws to a cycle low below 250,000 t, a second inventory pool now destocking across successive publications, and a front end that carried a backwardation into the new week. Buyers retain a restart running ahead of its own schedule and a Japanese currency near 159 to the dollar. For reference, Q3 opening offers ran $440-480/t and settled at $395/t, and the CIF Japan spot reference sits $25/t below the settled quarterly number.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW. The last edition carried here (06-August) had the SMM Imported Bauxite Index at $71.57/mt, up $0.70 week-on-week, with Guinea CIF at $70-74/mt and Guinea FOB at $38-42/mt. Bauxite is the identified core driver of the rise in Chinese alumina full production cost and remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on this board - the structural cost pressure that survives the Alunorte resolution entirely, because it is about ore supply and freight rather than one refinery's gas contract. The August Guinea long-term contract remains under negotiation against July's $70-71.5/mt settlement, and Guinea's move to monthly spot tenders through state-owned Nimba Mining adds price discovery while shifting volume from contract to spot. Today's Jamaica-Ghana tolling proposal is a third data point in the same direction: the industry is re-routing around concentrated ore supply.

THE PERMANENCE OF THE ALUNORTE GAS ARRANGEMENT. Norsk Hydro's own language is that the terminal-access agreement with CELBA is TEMPORARY, alongside ANP approval for the refinery to act as a self-importer of natural gas. The outage is resolved on a run-rate basis but the underlying gas supply arrangement is not permanently settled, and a 6.3 Mt/y refinery is large enough that any recurrence is material to the seaborne alumina balance. The thing to watch is a further company disclosure converting the temporary arrangement into a durable one - or failing to. Note also that no public seaborne alumina print dated after 07-August has appeared across six runs, so the entire episode passed without registering on any price series available here.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - AND THE RESEARCH HOUSE THAT SAID SO REPEATED IT VERBATIM THIS MORNING. SMM's 17-August minutes restate that 18% of the Gulf smelter's 1,262 pots have restarted, that the pace of resumption is FASTER THAN THE MARKET PREVIOUSLY EXPECTED, and that the previously traded tight-supply premium faces giveback pressure with upside room capped by resumption expectations. That sits on top of the dated entries already logged - Q1-2027 Gulf recovery guidance, the Australian smelter power settlement covering up to 590,000 t/y, Alunorte's return to full rate, Slovalco's 75,000 t/y in Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals' 75,000 t/y before year-end, and Mount Holly at full capacity adding nearly 10% to US primary output. TREND UP, HIGH IMPACT: this is not a forecast, it is a published schedule that is reported to be running ahead of itself, and the market has already taken $125.00 out of the price on its first entries.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPS OR REVERSES AND REMOVES THE BULL CASE'S BEST EVIDENCE. Seven weeks of consecutive LME draws to 248,300 tonnes are the single strongest public argument for tightness, and the argument dies the day metal starts returning to warrant. TREND DOWN, AND THE EVIDENCE AGAINST THIS RISK EXTENDED FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE PUBLICATION. SMM's 17-August minutes put Chinese aluminium ingot inventory in the major consumption regions at 886,000 tonnes as of Monday, down 12,000 tonnes from last Thursday and down 31,000 tonnes from last Monday, following 898,000 tonnes reported on Thursday. Two structurally different pools drawing together across successive publications is a run rather than a reading, and the standing objection - that exchange stock can fall for financing reasons unrelated to consumption - does not travel to Chinese social inventory. THE HONEST CAVEAT IS UNCHANGED: the lower stock goes, the more consequential any single delivery-in becomes, and SMM's own expectation is that the destocking pace narrows.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED. Day 169 since the shutdown. The most recent public restatement, in SMM's 16-August review, has the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council saying the Strait will remain closed unless the United States changes its behaviour, with reopening conditional on the US meeting FIVE conditions including a permanent halt to military operations; the US President is separately reported as preferring economic pressure to another large-scale military operation, and Iran's Foreign Minister says there are no negotiations under way though mediators continue trying. NOTHING DATED 17-AUGUST CHANGED ANY OF THAT. TREND FLAT: the Strait is still shut and the substance is unchanged. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production pre-conflict, and last week demonstrated the calibration - repricing three individual assets moved this market 3.7% in three sessions, so a change in the Strait regime itself would be an order of magnitude larger in either direction.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL - AND THIS RUN ADDED THREE SEPARATE DATED DATA POINTS ON THAT SIDE. First and most mechanical: China's July aluminium billet operating rate hit a year-to-date high of 58.3%, but SMM reports billet processing fees have fallen BELOW the industry's average production cost line, some producers have already suspended or cut output, and the August rate is expected to retreat to around 56.9% - and negative billet conversion margins divert metal back into ingot exactly when inventory statistics are being read as proof of tightness. Second: CPCA data put China's July passenger vehicle retail at 1.461 million units, down 20.9% year-on-year, with internal combustion down 41% and NEV down 3.9%, partially offset by a 147.8% year-on-year surge in NEV exports. Third: US July retail sales fell 0.6% month-on-month with the core control group at its worst since January 2025. TREND UP: three independent demand-side prints in one run, in the world's two largest consuming economies, at a price level $88.50 above the July swing low.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. This desk argued for a week that a rally making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium was carried by expectation rather than prompt need, and $125.00 has now come out of the price in three sessions. TREND DOWN, AND THE FIRST DIRECT EVIDENCE ARRIVED THIS MORNING: SMM reports that in Friday's LME session trading volume pulled back while OPEN INTEREST INCREASED, which it characterises as bulls adding positions rather than length liquidating; on SHFE the mirror image, with open interest falling on bears reducing positions. Set against a front end that held a backwardation through a $60 two-session decline and carried it into the new week, the weight of evidence is against a disorderly unwind. The residual exposure is materially lower than it was at $3,374.00 and the liquidation has not damaged the prompt structure.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND DOWN. The Alunorte gas disruption - the only credible alumina cost threat of the year - resolved in three days via ANP self-import approval and a temporary CELBA terminal-access agreement, with lost production of 100,000-120,000 t against a roughly 145 Mt/y global market and no public seaborne price print produced at any point. The Gulf producer's alumina refinery separately recovered to 50% of pre-incident capacity in early July, so alumina supply is being restored from two directions at once. The carried FOB East Australia mark of $356/mt is about 11.0% of the 14-August three-month price against a decade rule of thumb of 15-17%, so alumina remains a clear tailwind to smelter margin. THE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE WORD 'TEMPORARY' IN THE CELBA AGREEMENT - the gas arrangement is not permanently settled - and the longer-run risk is upstream of the refinery rather than in it, which is the thread running through the Guinea contract negotiations, the 749% year-on-year surge in Chinese alumina imports reported for H1-2026 and the Jamaica-Ghana tolling proposal disclosed today.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE MONTHLY SETTLEMENT WINDOW OPENS TODAY. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle around the 17th-18th, and all three rows are carried at their June or July cycles because no newer public mark exists. Two things point the settlement upward: Brent closed 14-August up 1.67% at $88.52 and green coke is a refinery by-product whose price follows crude with a lag; and the fluoride lines have ALREADY moved, with SMM's 16-August fluoride weekly lifting cryolite quotations to RMB 7,500-9,000/t from RMB 7,000-8,500/t, holding aluminium fluoride at RMB 11,200-11,800/t, and reporting the August AlF3 tender price of the benchmark Chinese aluminium enterprise raised RMB 250/t month-on-month on 97% fluorite consolidating firm at RMB 3,300-3,750/t. European gas closed up 1.70% at EUR 61.43/MWh. TREND UP: a firm carbon settlement this week would make it two cost groups turning against smelters in the same fortnight, at a moment when the metal has given back $125.00 from its high.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. China alone ran a 322 kt deficit in June, and exchange inventory at a fresh century low leaves no absorption capacity

Consensus expects surpluses as Gulf output recovers and Indonesia ramps; Concord Resources warns the market may be 'too complacent about supply risks' in the meantime. Rio Tinto's 40% Yarwun alumina cut from October 2026 trims one input to that surplus REVIEWED 13-AUG: no balance-relevant datapoint changed on 12-August. Exchange inventory drew for a 31st consecutive session, 1,700 t to 251,700 t, and the draw rate ACCELERATED from the 1,500 t/day that had run for six of the seven prior sessions - the tightening in visible metal continued on a day the price fell 1.94%. Against that, Alunorte remains at 50 percent with roughly 3 Mt/y of seaborne alumina out, which is an upstream cost event rather than a metal balance event and should not be double-counted as a supply deficit for primary aluminium.

caveats: PUBLIC SOURCES ONLY. Every figure and claim on this dashboard traces to a public source with a URL attached. Nothing confidential, internal or company-specific to any operator is published here - no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is public listed-company information in the peer-earnings and producer-status panels, which cite company releases or press coverage of them.

THERE IS NO 17-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL YET AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THIS PAGE. This compiles on MONDAY 17-AUGUST-2026 BEFORE THE 13:20 LONDON RING. The 14-August official is therefore the latest published settlement for every metal, and every LME number here is identical to yesterday's because no newer session exists - not because a fetch was skipped. The next genuine price information arrives at 13:20 London today.

THE WHOLE BOARD IS ON ONE UNIFORM SESSION. All six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings belong to 14-August (EUR/USD MTLE 1.15660, ECB 1.15670, BFIX 1.15662 - three independent fixings within four ten-thousandths of each other). No figure has been mixed across sessions.

CACHE CROSS-CHECK, KEPT REGARDLESS OF THE RESULT: the cache-busted ENGLISH overview and the cache-busted GERMAN overview were both fetched this run and both returned the same 14-August board. That is the FIFTH fully clean cross-check in a row, against four logged cache incidents earlier in the cycle (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables, 12-Aug English overview). The check is retained because the runs on which it would have mattered are not knowable in advance.

SECOND-SOURCE CORROBORATION THAT NO NEWER PRINT EXISTS. Trading Economics' independent CFD series still marks aluminium at $3,247.70 for 14-August. SMM's 17-August minutes separately give the 14-August LME session as open $3,238.50, high $3,260.00, low $3,221.50, close $3,245.00 on its own basis - a different series from the 13:20 official and quoted as such, not blended with it.

SPREAD CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above 3-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3-month is CONTANGO. On 14-August cash settled $3,248.00 against a three-month of $3,246.00, a $2.00 BACKWARDATION. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS across 13 and 14-August - the flat price fell $60.00 while the front end stayed in premium - which is called out because it is the single most informative feature of the board.

PROPORTION ON THE SPREAD: $2.00 is 0.06% of cash and half of the prior session's $4.00 premium. The correct words are 'the front end held its premium', not 'the market is in steep backwardation'. Copper's $411.00 prompt premium on the same session is the scale against which aluminium's should be read.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. Every premium row carries its last public mark at its assessment date, stated in the row. A dedicated search this run returned no aluminium premium assessment dated after those marks for MJP spot, EDU Rotterdam, Rotterdam billets or the US Midwest. Nothing was rolled forward, re-dated or estimated.

THE MJP Q4-2026 FIGURE IS A SCENARIO RANGE, NOT AN ASSESSMENT, AND IT IS HELD UNCHANGED AT $305-395 THIS RUN. No public producer offer, negotiation level or settlement coverage dated after the 06-July Q3 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan has been located. The range was narrowed yesterday on SMM's statement that the Gulf restart is running faster than expected; today SMM restated that characterisation verbatim, and a repetition is not new evidence, so the range is held rather than moved again.

THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT AN ASSESSMENT. The Section 232 leg shown is the re-verified 50% rate on aluminium articles multiplied by the LME cash settlement; the residual is the balance against the published US duty-paid premium row. It is not a freight, financing or tightness split and must not be read as one.

THE ALUMINA PANEL IS UNCHANGED FOR A SIXTH RUN BY DESIGN. No public seaborne alumina price print dated after 07-August has been located, so no value on that panel was changed, re-dated or estimated. Each row states its own assessment date.

INPUT-BASKET HISTORIES ARE NEVER INTERPOLATED AND GAPS STAY GAPS. No row gained a new sourced mark this run - the fluoride marks appended yesterday from SMM's 16-August weekly are carried, and no fresher public assessment dated 17-August was located for any row. The copper row's 15-session window did not roll because no new LME official has been published. Three rows - smelter electricity, cathode and graphite blocks, and titanium-boron grain refiner - carry empty histories because no public series exists at a consistent basis, and their source fields say so.

EARNINGS HISTORIES CONTAIN EXACT PUBLISHED FIGURES ONLY AND GAPS ARE LEFT AS GAPS. One company was rebuilt this run directly from its own results release, replacing two figures that did not match the primary disclosure and adding a third exact point from the same table. A separate check for a Chinese major's H1-2026 result was run and deliberately NOT published: the search result located was dated August 2025, describes H1-2025, and is arithmetically inconsistent with that company's already-published Q1-2026 actual.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE SECTION IS TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE. The count is unchanged and has not been re-labelled, and could not have been: no new session has printed since the last confirmed pivot. All plotted pivots are confirmed historical prices and the weekly and daily charts share the same pivots at the same prices. The stated invalidation is a decisive daily close below 3,229.50.

THIRD-PARTY PRICE RANGES ARE QUOTED AS CALIBRATION, NOT AS THIS DASHBOARD'S FORECAST. SMM's published week-ahead range is LME aluminium $3,180-3,330/t and RMB 23,600-24,450/t on the most-traded SHFE contract, and its 17-August note flags the 20-day moving average near $3,243.86. These are attributed third-party numbers and are neither endorsed nor blended into any figure on this page.
THE MODEL BAND, SENTIMENT SCORE AND FORWARD BLOCK ARE ENGINE-GENERATED from the published price history and are not hand-authored. Third-party model or consensus numbers are attributed where quoted.

NO EXCEL ARCHIVE IS PRODUCED ON THE DAILY RUN. A dated Excel archive is generated by the separate weekly task. This run refreshed DATA ONLY - the front end is a static, human-reviewed artefact and was not rebuilt.
